focus: Adversarial verification of the recommended one-lineage refusal: which legitimate callers the predicate would wrongly refuse, and what that forces in the change set
noveltyJustification: 4 of 8 findings are fully new (an in-tree packet config holding a one-entry matrix, the absence of any persisted-matrix reader on the resume path, the required amendment of the doc trigger sentence, and the flag needing two homes), 4 are partially new (count-expansion equivalence, the second council exclusion proof, fixture verification plus the house refusal precedent, and the unconditional status write that closes a carried-forward question).
ruledOut: A distinct-base-label guard: replica expansion makes it refuse the documented single-executor --count>1 native fan-out path
Guarding resume by re-validating a persisted fanout.executors: no code reads that field, so the reader would create the surface it polices
Making single-lineage refusal a per-executor-kind rule in the workflow YAML only: one layer above the direct script call that caused the incident

label: The one-lineage predicate is correct only because replica expansion runs first: expandLineages keeps count:1 as one lineage and expands count>1 into label-1..label-N, so allLineages.length<2 and "fewer than two expanded labels" coincide and a single --executor X --count 5 passes both. A distinct-base-label rule would refuse that documented native fan-out path.

The one real false positive already exists in-tree: the per-prompt-injection-audit research packet persists a fanout.executors matrix of length one (sol, iterations 15), so re-invoking it after the guard lands is refused unless --allow-single-lineage is passed. A genuine two-lineage packet (mimo + deepseek) is unaffected.

No persisted-matrix resume path exists to guard: resume is decided inside phase_init (on_resume branch), the fan-out matrix is a render-time binding from invocation flags, and no runtime script reads a stored fanout.executors. A lineage child is marked by config.fanout_lineage_artifact_dir plus a fanout block with {label, concurrency, siblingLineage} and no executors key.

The council is refused by code before expansion: ACTIVE_FANOUT_LOOP_TYPES is {research, review} and assertActiveFanoutLoopType throws inputError otherwise, so the loop-type conjunction in the new predicate is an intent-documenting optimization rather than a load-bearing council safeguard.

The escape flag is mandatory, not optional: three stress cases (fanout.vitest.ts:165,756,794) invoke the CLI with a one-entry executor array and pin one shim capture each, so a second entry weakens the assertion. No unit suite passes executor matrices to the CLI, so the fixture cost is confined to the stress suite.

The repository already ships this refusal one layer up: the research YAML refuses cli-deepseek-harness on the non-fan-out branch with "rerun with --count=2 or a second --executor group, or choose another executor kind" followed by process.exit(2), failing closed before any dispatch receipt. That is the wording and shape the new inputError refusal should reuse.

Change 2 must amend the doc trigger sentence, not append to it: research.md and review.md currently declare "an --executors value" (one-entry included) as fan-out, which the guard would refuse, so the trigger has to be restated as two or more expanded lineages in both command docs and both presentation policy lines.

The carried-forward status question is answered: step_update_config_status has no skip_when and sits in phase_synthesis, which every fan-out branch reaches (research 1053/1056/1059, review auto 420/1105-1111, review confirm 408), so a correct fan-out run does write status complete at packet level. The field is a safe post-hoc discriminator that cannot false-positive a correct run, and still only fires after the damage.
A refusal added to fanout-run.cjs must leave every documented fan-out shape (two or more --executor groups, --count above 1, multi-entry --executors) accepted after replica expansion.
Code and command docs must agree on the fan-out trigger sentence; a guard that refuses a call the docs declare legal is incomplete until the sentence is amended.
